correctness.rationale: An exact Hamming-slice decomposition bounds the zero, singleton, and multi-success contributions with second factorial moments, yielding the finite rare-event expansion. A one-disagreement decomposition yields the proxy expansion. Coordinate swaps preserve lambda_i and a_i exactly while changing the signed intensity, proving the factor-two family and its estimator consequences.

originality.rationale: Recent work gives universal proxy bounds and small-parameter multiplicative estimates, while earlier tensorization work gives a related obstruction from marginal TV data. Targeted searches did not locate the additive signed-mass expansion, the exact same-(lambda_i,a_i) factor-two construction, or the resulting sqrt(2) and 1/3 barriers. Older rare-event and Poisson-binomial asymptotic literature remains a residual risk, so the claim is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result identifies the first-order statistic lost by a new efficiently computable TV proxy, supplies a finite-sample quantitative correction, and proves a sharp representation-level information-loss example with explicit approximation barriers.
